correctness.rationale: Prime-root classes modulo p number phi(p-1). Exactly p lifts per such class modulo p^2 are squarefree. Thus r_p=p^2-1-p phi(p-1) is exact, including p=2. CRT with Möbius squarefree divisor inversion gives S_N=N B(y)/zeta(2)+O(Q(y)^2 sqrt(N)); all errors absolute and uniform. PNT controls Q; all survival factors are >=1/3 at p=2 and >=1/2 at odd primes, hence relative asymptotics for y<=(1/4-eps)log N. The correction factors differ from one by at most 2/(p^2-1), proving positive convergence. Exact residue and numeric calculations are independently re-evaluated in VERIFY.py; finite checks are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Squarefree inputs form a canonical positive-density class singled out in work on least Artin primes. The theorem quantitatively shows that conditioning on failure at increasing prime moduli changes the squarefree prevalence from 1/zeta(2) to K/zeta(2) and determines the exact persistent correction K in a uniform logarithmic cutoff range. This distinguishes a genuine arithmetic dependency not captured by unrestricted CRT probabilities; it is a structural distribution theorem, not a finite table, generic renaming, or an arbitrary parameter slice.
